entities.title: Cached results miss ignore-rule changes outside the visited directories
entities.summary: A cached search, list or outline is reused after a change to .git/info/exclude, the global git excludes file, or a .gitignore or .ignore in a parent of the search root, although the walk honours all of them.
entities.expected: A repeated search, list or outline reflects the ignore rules in force now, as a fresh walk would.
entities.observed: walk::builder enables git_exclude, git_global and parents, but the cached result's dependencies stamp only the visited files and directories and each visited directory's .gitignore and .ignore (walk::ignore_file_deps); .git is never entered. An edit to any other ignore source leaves every stamp equal, so State.cached reuses the old result until something stamped changes; fresh: true does not help, because it only re-sends the cached content.
reproduction: In a git working tree, create an untracked file holding a word, wait more than 2 seconds, start `afs jsonl` and search for the word.
Add that file's name to .git/info/exclude (or to a .gitignore in the directory above the search root).
Run the same search with fresh: true: the reply has cached: true and still lists the file.

origin.description: Found by reading walk.rs, search.rs, list.rs, outline.rs and state.rs; not reproduced by running afs.

entities.title: Dirty sets from file-system events
entities.summary: Use inotify or fanotify (Linux) and FSEvents (macOS) to know which files changed, instead of re-stat-ing every dependency.
entities.details: Planned, but absent until a benchmark justifies it; staleness is detected by re-stat instead (decisions.json, restat-not-watchers).
acceptanceCriteria: A benchmark shows re-stat cost worth removing.
Results stay equal to a full scan.

entities.title: Hand-written assembly for the hot loops
entities.summary: Hand-written assembly for byte scanning, planned but absent until a benchmark justifies it.
entities.details: The README stated that the compiler-vectorised memchr (with runtime-detected SIMD) already saturates memory bandwidth on the hot loops.
acceptanceCriteria: A benchmark shows a hot loop that memchr and the regex crate do not already run at memory bandwidth.
